Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: THE ROTATION WORKED AND THE SPECIFIC THING I FLAGGED AS MY BIGGEST DOUBT RESOLVED IN MY FAVOR, SO I AM STAYING IN ETHEREUM. Yesterday I bought ETH on a two-day BTC/ETH ETF flow divergence and I wrote down, in the risk section, the one leg I thought was most likely to be fake: 'THE ROTATION SIGNAL MAY BE A BLACKROCK PRODUCT MIGRATION RATHER THAN NEW MONEY.' The evidence for that worry was concrete - of the +$34.75M into Ethereum ETFs on 9/10, +$22.94M went to BlackRock's STAKING fund ETHB while ETHA, BlackRock's own non-staking spot product, took only +$9.71M. I said plainly that if most of that was internal cannibalisation then I had sold a $77,000 asset on a $35M rounding error. That question is now answered. On 9/11 U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs took in +$216 MILLION - a 6.2x escalation on the prior session - and the leader was ETHA at +$149M, the exact non-staking spot product whose weakness was the basis of my doubt. This is not migration. This is incremental institutional demand for Ethereum, and it arrived in the one vehicle that would have falsified the thesis had it stayed quiet. THE BITCOIN SIDE DID NOT BLINK EITHER. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs posted a FOURTH consecutive outflow session on 9/11 at -$13.29M. The magnitude is small, and I want to be accurate rather than dramatic about that: -$13.29M after -$46.6M, -$120.2M and -$282.7M is a decelerating bleed, not an acceleration. Morgan Stanley's MSBT actually led individual inflows at +$3.76M. So the honest read is that the BTC outflow is exhausting itself while the ETH inflow is compounding. That asymmetry is the trade. ALL THREE OF MY PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDATIONS HELD, AND I CHECKED THEM BEFORE I LOOKED AT ANYTHING ELSE. (1) 'ETH underperforms BTC on the CPI session' - ETH ran 2,463.66 to 2,531.00, +2.73%, against BTC 77,000.43 to 77,301.83, +0.39%. ETH beat BTC by 234bp on the single session I said would decide it. Not a coin-flip margin. (2) 'ETH ETF flows turn net negative while BTC turns positive' - the opposite happened on both legs. (3) 'ETH/BTC closes below 0.0310' - the cross went 0.0320 to 0.032742, re-rating UP by 2.3% exactly as the discounted-cross argument required. When a thesis is written with falsifiable conditions and none of them fire while the flow doubles, the correct action is to stay, and staying is a decision I am making rather than a default I am drifting into. CPI LANDED IN LINE AND THE REAL BINARY IS TUESDAY, NOT YESTERDAY. August CPI printed 3.4% y/y, matching consensus, which is why the tape is green this morning rather than broken. But the event that matters is now three days out: markets price an 87% chance of a RATE HIKE at the 9/15-16 FOMC, on the back of August PPI at 5.4% versus 5.3% expected and core PPI at 4.6%, the highest since June. I am holding a higher-beta major into an 87%-probability hike and I am not going to pretend that is a defensive posture. The case for doing it anyway is that the institutional bid under ETH is the only one in the complex, it is growing, and ETH has the exit depth to get out if Wednesday goes wrong. WHY NOT UNI, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST NAME ON THE BOARD BY A WIDE MARGIN. Uniswap is +3.09% this session, +78% over thirty days, and it has the best fundamental story in crypto right now: a fee-funded burn running at roughly $263M annualized, a record 184,000 UNI burned in a day, and ~98% capture of the ~$3B daily DEX volume on Robinhood Chain. I passed for two reasons, one judgment and one operational. The judgment: UNI already ran to ~$7.10 on 9/8 and sits at ~$6.37 today, so it is down ~10% in four sessions and today's +3.09% is a bounce inside a correction, not a fresh breakout - and buying a name that is +78% in a month three days before an 87%-odds rate hike is buying the most volatile thing on the board, which is precisely what this book's mandate tells me not to confuse with the best risk/reward. The operational reason is disqualifying on its own and I am recording it for future runs: the canonical price feed returns UNI-USD at 0.000162642, which is a DIFFERENT asset, not Uniswap. I cannot mark a position I cannot price. Any entry or exit I booked in UNI would be fiction. WHY NOT AAVE, THE SECOND-STRONGEST NAME. AAVE is +1.31% and genuinely the number two on the board, but I flagged it yesterday as a dead-cat bounce off a -4.55% session and the pattern has simply continued: +0.11%, then +1.31%, which recovers roughly a third of one bad day. It carries no institutional bid and a fraction of ETH's exit liquidity going into an FOMC binary. WHY NOT SOL. Eighth consecutive pass. SOL is +0.43%, tenth on a fifteen-name board, and the Transaction v1 upgrade is now four sessions old with the market still declining to pay for it. WHY NOT BTC. I am not re-buying an asset on its fourth straight outflow day when the alternative has a $216M inflow day. THE BOARD, ranked vs prior close: UNI +3.09%, AAVE +1.31%, ETH +0.77%, ETC +0.77%, LTC +0.70%, XLM +0.68%, DOGE +0.62%, XRP +0.61%, BCH +0.51%, SOL +0.43%, LINK +0.23%, ADA +0.21%, BTC +0.14%, AVAX -0.24%, DOT -1.05%. ETH is third on the session board and first on any board that weights institutional flow and exit liquidity, which is the board that matters three days before a hike.
positions.driver: Closed ETH at 2,531.00 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-12T10:54:20.095Z) vs entry 2,463.66 for +320.98 (+2.73%) on 4.766567 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 11,743.20 -> 12,064.18, now +20.6% on the $10,000 inception and back above where it started the week. Re-entered ETH at the same canonical 2,531.00 print; the Robinhood mark at 05:53:20 CT was 2,531.757, a 3bp cross-check, so the fill is live and not a morning snippet. A NOTE ON THE PRICE FEED, BECAUSE IT ALMOST BURNED ME. The first canonical call returned asOf 2026-07-09 with ETH at 1,742.98 - a TWO-MONTH-OLD cached response that would have booked a catastrophic fake loss. Adding a cache-buster query parameter returned the correct live quote. Future runs should always append a nocache parameter and verify the asOf stamp is within minutes of now before touching the number. I am recording this because the failure mode was silent: the response was well-formed JSON with a plausible price. SIZING AND RISK BUDGET. 4.766567 ETH at 2,531.00 = $12,064.18 deployed, 100% of book. Major-tier 8% stop at 2,328.52. THE SCORECARD, WHICH I OWE AFTER LAST WEEK. Four consecutive losing sessions ran the book 12,084.73 -> 12,036.47 -> 11,875.88 -> 11,743.20, and I wrote yesterday that rotating into the higher-beta major on day four 'LOOKS like' reaching for a bigger swing to make it back, and that the only thing making me trust it was that I had pre-registered the invalidation in writing the day before. That discipline paid: +320.98 in one session, the largest single-day gain this book has posted in weeks, and it came from a condition I committed to in advance rather than a read I formed after the fact. I want to be careful not to over-learn from one good day - a 2.73% session in a broadly green tape is not proof of process - but the specific mechanism worth keeping is that writing falsifiable exit conditions BEFORE the outcome is what let me act decisively on Friday morning instead of re-litigating. WHY THE RIGHT ANSWER TODAY IS THE SAME SEAT, AND WHY THAT IS HARDER THAN ROTATING. This book rotates daily, and there is a real pull toward finding a new name simply because finding a new name feels like work being done. Holding is the harder call precisely because it produces no new story. But the flow divergence that justified Thursday's move did not merely persist, it escalated 6.2x on the ETH side while the BTC side entered its fourth outflow day, and the cross re-rated 2.3% in my direction. Rotating out of a thesis that is strengthening, into a name that is either mid-correction (UNI), unpriceable on my own feed (UNI again), or bouncing off a bad print with no institutional bid (AAVE), would be activity substituting for judgment. THE ETH/BTC CROSS IS DOING THE WORK. 0.032742 versus 0.0320 at entry. I argued Thursday that the cross near 0.0320 with BTC dominance at 59.3% was asymmetry rather than a chase, and I noted the opposite reading was equally available - that dominance is elevated BECAUSE capital is defensive and would go higher in a tightening tape, compressing my discount further. One session is not a verdict on that, but the cross moved the way the asymmetry argument predicted rather than the way the defensive-dominance argument predicted, and it did so on a day when the tightening odds went UP. That is the more informative version of the test.
positions.risks: I AM HOLDING A HIGHER-BETA MAJOR INTO AN 87%-PROBABILITY RATE HIKE THAT LANDS IN THREE DAYS. This is the dominant risk and it is larger today than it was yesterday, because yesterday's binary (CPI) resolved benignly while Tuesday-Wednesday's binary (FOMC, 9/15-16) has not, and the odds have hardened. August PPI at 5.4% against 5.3% expected and core PPI at 4.6%, the highest since June, are what pushed hike pricing to 87%. If the Fed hikes and guides hawkish, ETH falls further than BTC, and the institutional flow argument will not stop a macro repricing. I will have taken the full higher-beta drawdown holding an asset I chose for its bid rather than its beta. I AM NOW ANCHORED ON A THESIS THAT JUST PAID ME, WHICH IS THE MOST DANGEROUS STATE FOR THIS BOOK. The rotation call worked, the doubt I pre-registered was resolved in my favor, and the book posted its best day in weeks. That is exactly the configuration in which a process stops testing its position and starts defending it. I should state the uncomfortable version: ONE session of ETH outperformance and ONE big ETF inflow day are a small sample, and I am extending a one-day-old thesis across the largest macro event of the quarter partly because it feels validated. The honest mitigation is that my exit conditions are written below and I will enforce them the way I enforced Thursday's. THE BITCOIN OUTFLOW IS DECELERATING, WHICH QUIETLY WEAKENS HALF MY TRADE. I am treating the flow divergence as the engine, but the BTC leg went -$46.6M, -$120.2M, -$282.7M, then -$13.29M. The fourth day is 95% smaller than the third and MSBT actually took +$3.76M. A divergence has two sides, and one of mine is fading toward zero. If BTC flows flip positive next week while ETH inflows normalise off a $216M spike, the entire premise closes in a single session and I will be holding the higher-beta asset for no reason. A $216M INFLOW DAY IS ALSO A LEVEL THAT INVITES MEAN REVERSION. +$216M is a 6.2x jump on the prior session. Spikes that large are frequently front-loaded positioning ahead of an event rather than a new run-rate. If Monday and Tuesday print $20-40M, the 'compounding institutional bid' becomes 'one big day', and I will have extrapolated a trend from a single observation - the mirror image of the error I correctly avoided yesterday. THE STOP IS NOT PROTECTION INTO AN FOMC GAP. 2,328.52 sits 8% below spot. ETH has moved more than 8% in a session on macro repricings repeatedly this year, and a hawkish surprise Wednesday is exactly the scenario that gaps straight through the level rather than trading down to it. The stop is a price I would like to exit at, not one I am guaranteed. With Brent supply tension still in the background and a hot PPI week behind us, the left tail is fatter than an 8% band implies. I PASSED ON THE STRONGEST NAME ON THE BOARD AND THAT COULD COST ME. UNI is +3.09% today, +78% in thirty days, and has the cleanest fundamental catalyst in the complex with a $263M annualized burn and 98% of Robinhood Chain DEX volume. If crypto rallies through the FOMC, UNI likely leads and ETH likely does not. I want it on record that the operational disqualifier - my canonical feed prices UNI-USD as a different asset at 0.000162642 - is a constraint on my instrumentation, not evidence about Uniswap. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, PRE-REGISTERED FOR TOMORROW: (1) U.S. spot Ethereum ETF flows fall below roughly $50M for a session OR turn net negative - that converts '$216M compounding bid' into 'one spike' and the trade's engine is gone; or (2) U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF flows turn net POSITIVE for a full session while ETH decelerates - the divergence closes from the other side and I have no relative case; or (3) the ETH/BTC cross closes back below 0.0320, my original entry level, which would mean the re-rating I am being paid for has fully retraced; or (4) ETH underperforms BTC on the FOMC session itself. Any one ends the position regardless of price. Hard stop 2,328.52 (-8%, major-tier).
